grammarItems.pattern: S + 姓 + surname；S + 叫 + name
grammarItems.explanationEn: 姓 is followed by a family name only. 叫 is followed by a given name or a full name. Use 姓 for "my surname is…" and 叫 for "I am called…".
是 links a person to a name or a nationality: 我是臺灣人. Nothing like "to be" is needed with 姓 or 叫, but 是 works with names and nationalities.
A question word takes the place of the answer and the word order does not change: 你叫什麼名字？ (compare 我叫明文).
有 means "to have" (or "there is"). Its negative is 沒有 (never 不有): 我沒有弟弟.
Add 嗎 to the end of a statement to turn it into a yes/no question: 你有弟弟嗎？
Counting people or things needs a measure word between the number and the noun. 個 is the general one: 一個弟弟. For two, use 兩個, not 二個.
grammarItems.matcher: [一兩二三四五六七八九十][個雙位杯家]

grammarItems.explanationEn: 也 means "also/too" and goes right before the verb, after the subject: 我也是臺灣人.
不 goes in front of a verb to make it negative: 我不是學生. It is read bú before a 4th-tone syllable and bù otherwise.
The place where something happens goes before the verb, introduced by 在: 我在銀行工作. This is the opposite of English word order.
grammarItems.matcher: 在.+(工作|念書|教|住|看|吃|打|跑)

grammarItems.explanationEn: 都 means "both/all" and sits before the verb, referring back to people or things already mentioned. 都不 means "none of them": 他們都不是學生.

grammarItems.pattern: S + V 不 V (O)？ / S + 有沒有 + O？
grammarItems.explanationEn: Repeat the verb with 不 between to ask a yes/no question: 你忙不忙？ With 有 the negative is 沒有: 你有沒有哥哥？ Don't add 嗎 as well.
呢 after a noun or pronoun means "and what about…?", returning a question you were just asked: 我叫小文，您呢？
的 links an owner to what is owned: 我的電腦. It is usually left out with close family: 我媽媽, 我爸爸.
The usual way to introduce someone: 這是我弟弟, then optionally their name: 這是我弟弟，王家文.
住在 means "live in/at" and takes the place straight after it: 他住在臺灣.

grammarItems.pattern: Question word in place of the answer (什麼 / 哪裡 / 誰)
grammarItems.explanationEn: 誰, 什麼 and 哪裡 stand where the answer would go, with no change in word order: 他在哪裡工作？ 誰住在臺北？
去 + place says where you go, and a second verb says what for. 想 ("would like to") goes before 去: 我想去法國念書.
grammarItems.matcher: 去.{0,12}(玩|念書|工作|看|吃|買|跑)

grammarItems.explanationEn: 還 adds a further action or item to what you just said ("also, in addition"): 我喜歡唱歌，還喜歡跳舞. It differs from 也, which adds another subject.
Chinese order: who, when, where, then what: 我晚上在家看電視.
grammarItems.matcher: (晚上|週末|每天|下午|平常|現在).*在.+(看|吃|跑|念|做|運動|打|聽|唱|跳|玩|工作|教|住)

grammarItems.pattern: S + 也 / 都 + (不 / 沒) + V
grammarItems.explanationEn: 也 and 都 come before the negative: 我們都沒有弟弟 ("none of us has…"). When used together the order is 也都: 他們也都有弟弟.
grammarItems.matcher: 也都|都不|都沒|也不|也沒

grammarItems.explanationEn: Numbers 11–99 are built from 十: 十二, 二十, 二十五. Use 兩 for "two" of something (兩個學生) and 二 when counting or in numbers.
grammarItems.matcher: [零一二三四五六七八九十百兩]|幾號

grammarItems.pattern: S + 給 + someone + 打電話
grammarItems.explanationEn: 給 marks who receives the call and goes before the verb: 我給你打電話. The person called comes before 打電話.
以後 after the first event means "after that…": 下課以後，我去吃飯. The earlier event comes first, as in English.

grammarItems.pattern: month 月 + day 號 / 日
grammarItems.explanationEn: Months are number + 月 (八月); days are number + 號 (十一號), or 日 in writing. Order is month first, then day.
grammarItems.matcher: [一二三四五六七八九十]+月|[一二三四五六七八九十]+[號日]

grammarItems.explanationEn: 幾 asks for a number: 今天幾月幾號？ asks the date, 你幾歲？ asks the age. Answer by putting the number where 幾 was.
Put 好不好 or 好嗎 after a suggestion to ask "is that OK?", and 可以嗎 to ask for permission: 我們去吃大餐，好不好？
grammarItems.matcher: 好不好|好嗎|可以嗎|可以不可以

grammarItems.explanationEn: Weekdays are 星期 + number, Monday = 一. Sunday is 星期天 or 星期日, never 星期七. 禮拜 means the same as 星期. Ask with 星期幾？

grammarItems.pattern: year 年 + month 月 + day 號
grammarItems.explanationEn: Dates run from big to small: year, month, day. Years are read digit by digit: 二〇二五年.

grammarItems.pattern: hour 點 + minute 分 / 半
grammarItems.explanationEn: Time is number + 點 (o'clock), then minutes + 分, or 半 for half past: 六點半. 分 can be dropped after the number.
grammarItems.matcher: [一二兩三四五六七八九十]+點|幾點

grammarItems.pattern: S + 跟 + someone + 一起 + V (O)
grammarItems.explanationEn: 跟…一起 means "together with…" and goes before the main verb: 我跟朋友一起吃飯.
得 after a verb introduces how well or how the action is done: 他說得很好. If the verb has an object, repeat the verb: 他說中文，說得很好.
有一點 (or 有點) means "a little" and is for unwelcome things: 有一點累, 有點難. It is not used with positive ones such as 好吃.
會 means "know how to" for a learned skill: 我會說中文. The negative is 不會.

grammarItems.pattern: S + V + 多少 / 幾 + (measure word) + N？
grammarItems.explanationEn: 多少 asks about any quantity (the measure word is optional); 幾 is for small numbers (up to about ten) and always takes a measure word: 你有幾個孩子？
